references.text: In [ref:Joh 4:54|John 4:54], the healing of the official's son is referred to as Jesus' 'second sign' performed in Galilee, pointing back to this first sign at Cana as the beginning of a series of signs.
[ref:Joh 1:14|John 1:14] speaks of the Word becoming flesh and us seeing his glory (δόξα). At Cana, Jesus revealed his glory through the first sign, thus fulfilling what the prologue promised.

In [ref:Joh 20:30-31|John 20:30–31], John summarizes that Jesus performed many signs (σημεῖα) which are written so that readers may believe. The wedding at Cana was the first of these signs, and its purpose—to stir up faith—is confirmed here already by the disciples' belief.
In [ref:Joh 11:40|John 11:40], Jesus tells Martha that she will see God's glory if she believes. The connection between signs, glory (δόξα), and faith is the same as at Cana.

In [ref:Joh 2:23|John 2:23], it is reported that many believed in Jesus' name when they saw the signs he performed during the Passover festival in Jerusalem. The disciples' faith at Cana was the first response to his signs.
In [ref:Joh 1:50-51|John 1:50–51], Jesus promises Nathanael that he will see greater things. The sign at Cana is the first fulfillment of this promise to the disciples.

[ref:Joh 6:14|John 6:14] reports that people saw the sign Jesus performed (the feeding miracle) and confessed him as the prophet who was to come. The signs in the Gospel of John, beginning with Cana, reveal Jesus' identity and lead to confession and faith.

[ref:Jes 25:6|Isaiah 25:6] describes the Lord's future feast with rich wine for all peoples. Jesus' turning of water into wine can be seen as a messianic sign pointing toward this eschatological abundance.

[ref:Jes 40:5|Isaiah 40:5] prophesies that the Lord's glory will be revealed. Jesus' revelation of his glory (δόξα) at Cana is part of this theme of God's manifestation of glory, even though its full fulfillment still awaits.

In [ref:Joh 12:37-38|John 12:37–38], John notes that the people did not believe despite all the signs Jesus had performed before them. This stands in contrast to the disciples' response of faith after the first sign at Cana.
